items.title: Parrish Skips Two Debates Monday as Crombie, Tedjo and Damerla Face Off Twice in One Day
items.summary: According to Insauga, three of Mississauga's four main mayoral candidates faced off twice on Monday while Mayor Carolyn Parrish sat out both events. Bonnie Crombie, Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla squared off Monday morning at the Mississauga Convention Centre in a housing-focused debate co-hosted by the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board and the Cornerstone Association of Realtors. The same three candidates were set to debate again Monday night at Mississauga City Hall, this time hosted by Policorner, an organization that covers politics and related news at Queen's Park. Insauga notes Parrish did not join her rivals at either event, despite telling the outlet back in July that she planned to take part in three debates before the Oct. 26 election. The housing debate asked candidates to lay out their visions for the city and address issues including affordability and housing supply.

items.title: Ontario's Solicitor General and Retail Council Leaders Join Peel Police's Two-Day Push Against Organized Retail Theft
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police are hosting a province-wide Retail Organized Crime Conference Tuesday and Wednesday at the Hyatt Place Toronto in Mississauga, bringing together law enforcement, retail industry leaders and public safety partners from across Ontario. Peel police said in a Monday news release that the two-day event aims to discuss emerging trends, investigative best practices and partnership-driven solutions to disrupt organized retail crime networks. Peel Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah, Deputy Chief Marc Andrews and Police Service Board vice-chair Omar Khan are set to welcome attendees including Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner and the Retail Council of Canada's Rui Rodrigues. Insauga reports Peel police formed a specialized unit in September 2025 dedicated to tackling break-ins and large-scale theft of goods such as jewelry and clothing from retail businesses. Deputy Chief Andrews said at a July press conference at Square One Shopping Centre that the force's increased focus on a crime he described as having become endemic in the community has paid off so far.

items.title: Jetliner Road Shut Down After Driver Strikes Pedestrian Near Pearson Airport Monday Morning
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel police say a pedestrian was taken to hospital Monday morning after being struck by a vehicle at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. Police did not release details about the pedestrian beyond confirming the injuries were minor. Investigators also did not disclose what kind of vehicle was involved in the collision. Police closed westbound Jetliner Road at Airport Road following the crash and asked drivers to find alternate routes. Officers did not say how long the closure would last. Insauga notes Monday's crash was the second time in less than a week that a pedestrian has been struck by a vehicle on a busy Mississauga road.

items.title: Milev Wins J/24 North American Title at Port Credit Without Taking a Single Race
items.summary: Rossi Milev of Canada and his team aboard Clear Air won the 2026 J/24 North American Championship, hosted by Port Credit Yacht Club in Mississauga from September 30 to October 4. According to Sail-World, Milev relied on consistency rather than a single dominant finish to take the title, never winning a single race across the eight-race series against a 24-boat fleet from the United States and Canada. The regatta came down to the final day, with just three points separating the top five teams heading into Sunday's racing. Sail-World reports the fleet faced an onshore postponement that morning before launching at noon, when the breeze settled into the southwest and built to 15 knots with gusts to 20. Milev's Clear Air had sat as low as ninth place at one point before climbing back into contention, finishing with a scoreline of 3-2-2-10-4-2-2-4 and 19 net points after discarding a 10th-place result. Canada's Evan Petley-Jones finished second overall aboard Lifted with 21 points, two behind the champion, while also topping the Corinthian division among the 18 Corinthian teams in the fleet. Kurt Dammeier's Amuse Bouche rounded out the podium in third with 22 points, one point behind Lifted.

items.title: Tedjo Doubles His Support Since August as Liaison Poll Shows Mississauga Mayoral Race Tightening to Three Ways
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a new Liaison Strategies poll conducted after last Thursday's debate found Mississauga's mayoral race tightening into a genuine three-way contest. Among decided and leaning voters, Bonnie Crombie came in at 30 per cent, Mayor Carolyn Parrish at 29 per cent and councillor Alvin Tedjo at 26 per cent, with Dipika Damerla at 11 per cent. David Valentin, principal at Liaison Strategies, told the Star the numbers show what is beginning to look like a three-way race. Valentin said Tedjo's climb may reflect undecided voters responding to the campaigns' bigger moves, pointing to Crombie's push for a subway extension and Tedjo's endorsement from the Peel Police union. He added that Tedjo's affordability-focused platform, including a proposed property tax freeze and a new deferral program for seniors, appears to be resonating given that affordability remains voters' top concern. The Star notes Tedjo sat at just 9 per cent in a similar Liaison poll taken in mid-August, when Crombie and Parrish were tied at 35 per cent among decided and leaning voters.

items.title: A Pandemic-Era Walk to a Mississauga Marsh Turned Into a Yearslong Conservation Mission for One Family
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Iyah, now a Mississauga tween, first noticed Osprey Marsh in the Lisgar neighbourhood back in fall 2020, when she was four years old and her family had just moved into the area during the pandemic. Iyah told the outlet the park's giant animal mural was impossible to miss from the car, and that it became one of the few places still open to her family while schools and activities shut down around them. She says she asked her mother, Jenna Evans, to take her to see it, and Evans agreed after weeks spent unpacking their new home. The Pointer reports the marsh sits a 10-minute walk from their house, near Ninth Line and Britannia Road West. Up close, mother and daughter found the animals painted on the mural were species that actually live in the marsh itself. That first visit marked the start of what has grown into Iyah's ongoing effort, years later, to protect the green space she found during one of the pandemic's quietest stretches.
